page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 3.1 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU allocation is dedicated, with hyper-threading enabled to provide 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1309.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1572.39. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform in the average range. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance falls into the weak category, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2855.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 4147.67. Memory bandwidth is relatively low, with uncached large block read and write speeds measured at 28.26 GB/sec and 24.11 GB/sec respectively.

This instance is best suited for workloads that rely heavily on single-threaded CPU performance rather than massive parallelization or high memory throughput. Appropriate applications include light web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale LLM text generation using lightweight models, where it achieves an average speed of 74.92 tokens/sec. It is less optimal for heavy database operations, software compilation, or complex physics simulations due to its weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth profiles.

Benchmarks reveal average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1309.0 and steady single-threaded decompression speeds, though multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are relatively weak. It is suited for single-threaded applications, light web serving, text processing, and small-scale language model text generation.
